I am a Robotics & R&D Engineer passionate about turning ideas into real-world robotic and intelligent systems.

At ROBOTWALA I work with Raspberry Pi 4/5 and help design and develop robotic systems, automation solutions and prototypes. A 3-month internship there grew into an R&D role based on my work.

I am also a 4th-year Electronics & Communication student at Acropolis Institute of Technology & Research. I took part in the Electronova and MSME hackathons, and served as Secretary of the IEEE AP-S Student Branch at AITR.

I believe in learning by building, solving real problems and pushing what the hardware can do.

Selected work

Featured engineering projects

Minor project

SCARA Robotic Arm

A 3D-printed 4 DOF SCARA arm that automates pick-and-place of small objects, and can be driven by hand gestures from a laptop camera.

  • Stepper-driven base, lift and arm joints with a servo gripper.
  • I wrote the control logic and the full project documentation.
  • A Python script on the laptop tracks my hand through the camera and sends moves to the arm.
4 DOFSTEPPERSPYTHONGESTURE CONTROL
Completed

Weather Monitoring & Control

A rooftop weather station built on an ESP microcontroller that reports temperature and humidity in real time over Wi-Fi.

  • Sensors sit in a radiation shield on a mast, wired down to the electronics.
  • A yellow enclosure with an LCD shows the live readings on site.
  • Automated control reacts to environmental conditions.
ESPWI-FISENSORSIOTLCD
Internship · Jul–Dec 2025

Toroid Coil Winding Machine

An Arduino-based machine that winds copper wire on toroidal cores, a job that is slow and inaccurate by hand.

  • Arduino Nano controls a 12V DC motor (L293D) that rotates the core.
  • A NEMA 17 stepper with an A4988 driver moves the wire feeder sideways for even layers.
  • An IR sensor counts turns live on a 16x2 I²C LCD, and a rotary encoder sets speed and direction.
  • Designed and fabricated the PCB myself.
ARDUINO NANONEMA 17PWMPCB DESIGN
Internship · Jul–Dec 2025

Smart Hydroponics System

An ESP32 system that monitors water quality and runs the pumps on a schedule, so plants grow with little manual work.

  • Reads a pH sensor and a TDS sensor, plus a DHT11 for air temperature and humidity.
  • DS3231 RTC over I²C turns the pumps on at set times.
  • ULN-driven relays switch the 230V and 12V pumps.
  • LCD shows time, pH, TDS and temperature every second. Custom PCB with a wiring flow I documented.
ESP32PH · TDSDS3231 RTCRELAYSI²C
Internship · Jul–Dec 2025

Colour & Shape Sorting Conveyor

A Raspberry Pi 5 conveyor that uses computer vision to sort objects, letting green items pass and diverting red ones.

  • Pi Camera captures frames as objects enter the inspection zone.
  • OpenCV finds colour in pixel colour spaces and shape with contour approximation.
  • A servo-driven gate sends each object to the right bin.
  • Belt driven by a DC motor through an L298N driver, with my own PCB.
